Qwen3.6-27B · block 56 · the same 587 whitespace-only thinking blocks, read by two lenses

Do the thinking-block scenes survive a different lens?

The catalog's readouts come from olens_s3d_rl600, which was trained only on assistant-reply positions. We re-read the same block-56 activations with that lens and with a variant continued-trained to also cover user tokens, chat-template tokens, empty and real thinking blocks, and post-reasoning replies (agastyasridharan/olens-qwen3.6-27b-userthink-s225). Re-running the original lens reproduces the catalog; the new lens almost never produces the watched, silent, laboratory scenes.

Category audit (same grader as the themes index)

gpt-5.4-mini with the themes index's frozen prompt and definitions; one readout per block per lens, graded blind in shuffled batches of four. “Catalog” is the saved label set. Most new-lens “obedience” matches are instruction-following language (“must adhere to the instruction”), not bowing or kneeling scenes.

Keyword themes and fit score

Regex themes over all readouts (English and Chinese patterns), averaged per block. “Template” rows are 192 empty blocks inserted by the native chat template (thinking disabled), 8 per setting × condition; the catalog does not cover them. Fit score is joint bullet FVE of a readout under a frozen phrase-to-activation reconstructor with a rebuilt whitener: low for both lenses at these positions, so neither readout set is shown to be faithful.

Method. Exact saved token IDs through the blank-line token; block-56 output with adapters disabled; injection of 16000·h/‖h‖ at the ㈜ marker; the study's carrier prompt, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, 256 tokens, seeded per position; same content guard. rl600 re-run: 4 readouts per block (one shown); new lens: 4 readouts (two shown). A second carrier (the lenses' one-line training prompt) gives the same picture. Readouts are lossy lens descriptions, not established internal states. Provenance and hashes.
